pages.text: The Akaishi Pulverizer is the first stop of the ore-processing line. Each grind takes 100 ticks at 15 energy/tick, with a 100k internal buffer; deepslate ores give the same result as normal ones.$(br2)$(bold)Akaishi line (two hops):$(0)$(li)Akaishi Ore (4 tiers x 4 environments) -> $(4)1 Compressed Akaishi Essence$(0)$(li)$(4)Compressed Akaishi Essence -> x2 Akaishi Dust$(0)$(br2)$(bold)Other ores (one hop):$(0)$(li)Coal / Iron / Gold / Diamond / Emerald / Quartz ore -> x2 matching dust$(li)Copper ore -> x3 Copper Dust$(li)Lapis ore -> x4 Lapis Dust$(li)Redstone ore -> x4 vanilla Redstone$(li)Ancient Debris -> 1 Netherite Dust$(li)Obsidian -> 1 Obsidian Dust

Dust is the machine line's $(4)universal middleman$(0): press it back into blocks with the Compressor, or turn it into bases with the Transformer.$(br2)$(bold)Two things to remember:$(0)$(li)Obsidian Dust and Netherite Dust have $(e)no vanilla smelting route$(0) — to recover Obsidian or Netherite Ingots you must pulverize first and then compress$(li)Lapis, copper and redstone give the fattest yields (3-4 per ore) — feed those ores here first$(br2)Connect item pipes to auto-feed ores and pull dust out, and you've got a hands-off ore-processing start.

After pulverizing: press blocks with $(l:akaishi:compressor)Compressor$(/l), make bases with $(l:akaishi:transformer)Transformer$(/l), or browse the list in $(l:akaishi:dusts)Dusts$(/l). Ore sources are covered in $(l:akaishi:ore)Akaishi Ore Clusters$(/l).
